The phase diff changes .github/workflows/ci.yml (a new select job, a new matrix job, and two service containers), apps/sales-advantage/cloudbuild-traffic.yaml (a step that captures a Cloud Run revision and a step that moves production traffic), apps/sales-advantage/scripts, and docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md. summary: The Phase 3 security review passes at 57bb8376c with four nonblocking findings and no blocker. The new select job takes BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA through env and quotes them. The script accepts 40-hex ids only. No workflow holds a secret, a pull_request_target trigger, or a write-all permission. Both service containers and the test credentials are identical to the phase base and point at localhost. The sales traffic file now moves traffic with --to-revisions to a candidate revision that the script verifies against the _PUSH_BUILD_ID image digest and against the latest-created revision. The move reads no tag and no legacy-rollback record, and the legacy record is deleted before the move. No workflow references a traffic file, and no push file holds a database step. A2 is not applicable and A6 has no hit.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Major] review-b: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 257 puts ${{ matrix.id }} into the shell line unquoted. The id comes from scripts/ci/apps.json at the checked-out commit, which is the pull request head on a pull_request event. scripts/ci/affected-apps.mjs readTable (line 346) checks only that id and path are strings, and scripts/ci/__tests__/ci-workflow.test.mjs line 177 checks only a non-empty string. A newline or a semicolon in an id breaks the line and runs another command, and a turbo flag in an id changes the filter. A charset check ^[a-z0-9-]+$ in the script or in the select step closes the path. Rationale: an untrusted value must not reach a shell line. The impact is bounded: a pull request already runs its own code through pnpm install and the tests, and ci.yml holds no secret. The token scope is the remaining risk (F2).

F2 [Major] review-b: .github/workflows/ci.yml declares no permissions block on any job (lines 1-257). test-strategy.md Q16 assigns ci.yml to Phase 3, and the P3 review bullet names the permissions block. The workflow reads the repository and needs contents: read only. Every step of packages and affected runs repository code with the repository default token scope. Rationale: least privilege. No secret is reachable, so the impact is bounded. With F3, a moved action tag would run with that token.

F3 [Nit] review-b: .github/workflows/ci.yml adds five uses lines that float on a major tag: actions/checkout@v4 (lines 32 and 238), actions/setup-node@v4 (lines 37 and 246), and pnpm/action-setup@v4 (line 241). Phase 2 Review B finding N5 recorded the two CD workflows pinning all ten uses lines to 40-hex commits. Rationale: a moved tag changes the code that runs with the job token.

F4 [Nit] review-b: apps/sales-advantage/cloudbuild-traffic.yaml migrate-db (lines 19-26) applies migrations from the source that the operator uploads with gcloud builds submit. No step compares that source with _RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA. apps/sales-advantage/scripts/verify-sales-release-inputs.mjs validateReleaseInputs checks the commit form and the backup description only. The push file runs release-source-manifest.mjs verify; the traffic file does not. Rationale: a dirty working tree can apply migrations that differ from the release commit. This predates Phase 3 and every run waits on Daniel's word.

F5 [Nit] review-b: docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md lines 13-14 state that each traffic file sends 100 percent of the traffic to the tag of the new revision and never names a revision. Phase 3 changes the sales file to --to-revisions with a captured revision name, so the global rule is false for sales-advantage and contradicts the sales section at lines 155-157. Rationale: the runbook must state what the file does. A scoped exception for sales-advantage in the global rule removes the contradiction.
evidence: Provenance: phase_base_sha 25d774e08a0f9bef8074fb6f88bde439d1a72066 resolves, and git cat-file -e 25d774e08:measure/tracks/per_app_cicd_20261107/test-strategy.md succeeds. role_base_sha and audited_head_sha are 57bb8376c1193988f907e4d0fd56ef6dd7eef23d. HEAD is eae1280274eae643a1fbde43c5869c14df2e4329, one commit later, and the diff over the phase paths is empty.

Scope: git log 25d774e08..57bb8376c lists this track's commits 6ba8f6696, 2cec361da, b7c8952a6, f0284be4e, e0cf21a1f, acc5f59d2, and 57bb8376c. The same range holds other tracks' commits (storytime_at_home_release_20261106, primary_storytime_removal_20261107, storytime_app_rebuild_20261025). This audit reads this track's paths only.

ci.yml permissions: git show 57bb8376c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | grep -E 'permissions|secrets\.|pull_request_target' exits 1. scripts/ci/__tests__/cd-workflows.test.mjs asserts a contents: read block for cd-www-reading-advantage.yml and cd-apps.yml only. No test covers a ci.yml permissions block.

ci.yml untrusted input: the select step (lines 43-54) sets BASE_SHA to ${{ github.event.before || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} and HEAD_SHA to ${{ github.sha }} through env, then uses "$BASE_SHA" and "$HEAD_SHA" quoted. scripts/ci/affected-apps.mjs COMMIT_ID rejects a non-40-hex base or head with exit 2, which blocks git option injection. The matrix line writes JSON.stringify output, which keeps the output single-line. The affected job reads the matrix with fromJSON(needs.select.outputs.matrix).

ci.yml fail-closed: the run block uses the default bash -e shell, so a script exit 2 aborts the step. A failed select skips affected through needs. An empty matrix skips affected through if: matrix != '[]', and packages still runs the guards.

ci.yml containers: postgres:16-alpine and docker.io/bitnamilegacy/pgbouncer:1.23.1 are identical to the base file (base lines 34 and 47; head lines 65, 78, 199, and 212). Credentials are postgres/postgres. DATABASE_URL and COMPANY_IDENTITY_TEST_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL point at localhost only. COMPANY_IDENTITY_TEST_POSTGRES_CONTAINER takes job.services.postgres.id, not a secret. ci.yml holds no GCP secret and no production URL.

Sales capture: apps/sales-advantage/cloudbuild-traffic.yaml lines 95-102 call capture-sales-cloud-run-tag.sh as a bash argv list with no -c, so _PUSH_BUILD_ID is not parsed by a shell. The script (lines 43-60) derives expected_repository, requires a sha256 digest, and exits 1 unless the tagged revision is the latest created revision and runs <repository>@<digest>. It also requires the tag URL https://<tag>---. The output prefix is /workspace/.sales-company-candidate, outside the repository.

Sales move: lines 106-117 read only /workspace/.sales-company-candidate.revision, quote the value in --to-revisions="...=100", and hold no --to-tags and no reference to .sales-legacy-rollback. verify-repair-verify-legacy-rollback (line 88) deletes both legacy records before the candidate capture, so the legacy record cannot be read. A later push that moves the candidate tag makes the digest or latest-revision check fail, and set -euo pipefail stops the build before the move.
Sales substitution defaults: the traffic file holds no _PUSH_BUILD_ID default. gcloud fails a build that leaves it undefined, so the build fails closed.

F-19 static check: all 10 checks of scripts/ci/__tests__/cloudbuild-files.test.mjs F-19 hold on the file as read (legacy and candidate image equal the ${_PUSH_BUILD_ID} image, both captures precede the move, the candidate record is a distinct /workspace path, the move uses --to-revisions, and the negative legacy move text is rejected). The Green log records sales_build_identity=1 with 130 tests passed. This audit did not run the suite.

Runbook against the file: the step list at docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md lines 135-141 equals the file order (verify-curriculum-backup, migrate-db, doctor-check, build-curriculum-workspace-deps, seed-production-curriculum, verify-production-curriculum, runtime-db-contract, capture-legacy-rollback, verify-repair-verify-legacy-rollback, capture-company-candidate, update-traffic). The fail-closed sentence at lines 155-157 matches the script. The global tag rule at lines 13-14 does not match the sales file (F5).

No workflow reaches a traffic file: grep -rn cloudbuild-traffic .github/workflows exits 1, and grep -rnE 'update-traffic|--to-latest' .github/workflows exits 1. No apps/*/cloudbuild-traffic.yaml holds an on: or triggers: key (grep exits 1). apps.json cloudbuild values are push files only, and F-08 reads row.cloudbuild and asserts no database step, so a row pointed at a traffic file would fail that test.

No push path touches a production database: a grep for psql, migrate, and cloud-sql-proxy over the 9 non-excluded push files returns one hit, a comment in apps/workbooks/cloudbuild.yaml line 3. The one-off files cloudbuild-catalogue.yaml, cloudbuild-etl.yaml, and cloudbuild.continue-f5063222.yaml are not workflow targets and are not table rows.

Known open limit, not raised as a finding: docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md lines 176-181 record that capture-legacy-rollback fails when the legacy-rollback revision is not the latest created revision, which holds after a push creates the candidate. That failure stops the build before capture-company-candidate. The runbook assigns the change to Daniel and the sales app owner. The record is the reason this audit does not raise it.

A2: the phase diff over the track paths holds no draft, published, consent, or anonymization token (grep exits 1). No test flips a named subject to published. The sales move is a deploy gate, not a publish gate.

A6: the A6 detector over measure/tracks.md exits 1. The per_app_cicd_20261107 row (line 76-79) says Phase 1 accepted and Phase 2 in review remediation. It claims no resolved security state. The plan note for 3.3a states the F-19 contract and does not claim a security state.

Not verified here, by role limit: no workflow ran, no gcloud read or write ran, no secret was read, and no test suite ran. Live IAM and the reduced www deploy key stay with Phase 4 task 4.7 and the P4 dry run.
